causes.text: Adobe announced it would acquire Figma for approximately $20 billion in cash and stock, raising concerns over the deal size, valuation, and future integration challenges.

source_info.title: Adobe to Buy Figma for About $20 Billion

effects.text: Adobe's stock dropped by 15% following the announcement of its $20 billion acquisition of Figma. Business Insider reported it on 2022-09-15.

source_info.title: Adobe Stock Price Drops 15% After $20 Billion Deal to Buy Figma

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2022-09-15, Adobe announced acquisition of Figma for $20 billion
Investors reacted negatively to deal value and dilution concerns
On 2022-09-15, Adobe stock fell 15% immediately following the news (on 2022-09-15)

rationale: The unusually high deal value and strategic uncertainty surrounding the Figma acquisition caused investors to question Adobe's capital allocation and competitive strategy, leading to a sharp sell-off.
counterfactual_analysis: Had Adobe not announced the Figma acquisition or proposed a lower valuation, the stock might not have experienced such a significant drop.

adversarial_confounders.text: General tech sector volatility during Q3 2022
adversarial_confounders.impact: May have contributed slightly, but the magnitude of Adobe's drop clearly links to the acquisition news.

details.commentary: Figma had become a fast-growing rival in collaborative design, intensifying competitive pressure on Adobe's creative software franchise. By paying a steep premium to acquire Figma, Adobe acknowledged that rivalry and signaled concern about defending its market position.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - A high-priced tech acquisition tested investor tolerance for risk
details.commentary: In a more cautious rate and valuation environment, a $20 billion deal for Figma raised doubts about capital discipline and future returns. Investors questioned whether the acquisition economics justified the price, triggering a sharp sell-off in Adobe's shares.
